action_summary: Every plan in this tree that proposed to 'wake the hidden organs' assumed the unimported modules were capabilities waiting for a caller. Nothing had ever checked, and a module nobody imports is not a capability, it is a claim. This PR adds an adjudicator: each candidate is imported in its own subprocess under a timeout, its unattended zero-argument self_check() is called if it has one, and the result is one of four fail-closed verdicts (PROVEN / IMPORTS_ONLY / MISSING_SUBSTRATE / BROKEN), with --no-probe as a built-in ablation. Measuring first corrected the premise: the candidate rule compared a bare filename stem against fully dotted import names, so every module reached as `from canonical.<pkg>.<mod> import X` counted as dark. The substantial no-importer bank is 227 modules, not 1,996. Adjudicating those 227 proves nothing: 0 can prove they run, 197 import and stop there, 28 need a package this repo does not ship, 2 are broken. The census over all 2,174 substantial modules finds 6 that can prove themselves, and 4 of the 6 got their self-check here -- including the 4,702-line semantic-causal engine, whose headline cross-language claim was silently false: statement-position C lowered to RAW_EXPR while Python lowered to RAW_STMT, so identical text sat in two opcodes and semantically_equivalent() returned False for programs the docstring said it collapses. Fixed at the statement-position fallback, and now proved by a positive cross-language pair, an inclusive-bound pair, a negative control that must NOT collapse, an idempotence check, and the emitted Python executed against a buffer.

expected_parent_change: The tree can answer 'which of your modules actually run' with a number instead of an assumption, and the answer is 6 of 2,174. Four organs carry executable proofs they did not have, and one of them had its own headline claim falsified by the proof and repaired.
expected_parent_frontier_change: Replaces 'we already have it somewhere' with a verdict per module. It removes the dormant-organ bank as a strategy (227 unproven modules cannot carry a wave) and moves the frontier's growth to the modules that can be made provable, which is what the next waves must be sized from.
falsification_condition: Falsified if a module recorded PROVEN fails its self_check() on a re-run, if the ablation produces a PROVEN verdict, if a third-party absence is counted as BROKEN or an in-repo import failure is counted as MISSING_SUBSTRATE, or if the corrected candidate rule still lists a module that some other module imports by dotted name.
honest_limits: PROVEN means one unattended self_check() passed in a subprocess. It is the module's own check; a weak check proves nothing and this instrument cannot tell a weak check from a strong one.
2,082 modules import cleanly and prove nothing. That is the largest number in the ledger and it is the point: none of it is evidence.
The dependency classifier files third-party absence as MISSING_SUBSTRATE rather than BROKEN, so a dependency that no longer exists anywhere is recorded as unexercisable rather than defective.
Four root3_* modules are BROKEN only in the sense that they do not finish importing inside 25 s; the budget is part of the verdict.
The first measurement of this wave used a wrong candidate rule (6,114 / 1,996). Those numbers are superseded and must not be quoted.
No claim of comparison to any published system: this is a census of this repository under its own contract.

load_bearing_primary.interpretation: Discharges nothing and unlocks little, on purpose: four modules that this PR shows cannot even be imported inside 25 s sit in the terminal execution path, and a module that cannot be imported cannot be dispatched. The bound is deliberately small because the census changes what the tree may claim about itself, not what it can do.

No-importer census: 227 candidates, PROVEN 0. Ablation (--no-probe): 227 candidates, PROVEN 0, IMPORTS_ONLY 227. The instrument's own self-check separates four fabricated modules into four states (5/5).
next_step: (1) Give a self_check to the next ten largest IMPORTS_ONLY modules in order of what a live path would use, one PR per three modules, since a contract that is not adopted is a wish; (2) make the census a CI gate so the PROVEN count can only rise deliberately; (3) treat the 4 root3_* import hangs as a real defect: a module that cannot be imported cannot be dispatched, and the federation cannot reach it.
real_outcome: 2,174 substantial modules adjudicated in 56 s: 6 PROVEN (7,479 lines), 2,082 IMPORTS_ONLY, 79 MISSING_SUBSTRATE, 7 BROKEN. The 227-module no-importer census proves nothing at all. The same run with --no-probe collapses all 227 into IMPORTS_ONLY, which is what the tree knew before. The quarantine is concrete: two modules do not parse, four root3_* modules never finish importing in 25 s, one self-check needs an argument and so is not callable unattended.

routes_considered.why: Adds the three missing operations by composition, and measures them against a from-scratch fixpoint oracle with a no-edges baseline and two controls.

Unification would be a larger capability, but the measured gap was three specific operations over ground facts; rewriting the store would also discard the cascade and diamond-preservation behaviour that already passes.
A protocol bench without the operations would score zero on its own hardest cases; measurement without acquisition adds no capability.
Retrieval cannot answer cascade or absence at any top-k; the baseline is included to show that, not to be improved.
